murari-kcc.title: Через Ренуку, Раджаграму и Гокулу — в Матхуру
murari-kcc.summary: Переправившись через Ямуну, Господь видит лес Агры, приходит в Ренуку — место Парашурамы, видит Ямуну, обращённую к Вриндавану, Раджаграму, Гокулу и Махавану и, наконец, Матхуру — место явления Кришны; Он смеётся, пляшет, плачет и катается по земле.

verses.text: С глубокими раскатами возгласов, весь в слезах любви и трепете, Он шёл всё дальше и, переправившись через Ямуну, увидел лес Агры<sup>*</sup>.
verses.orig:
हुङ्कारगम्भीरारावैः प्रेमाश्रुपुलकैर्वृतः।
व्रजन् क्रमात्तामुत्तीर्य वनं चाग्रं ददर्श ह॥३॥
verses.translit:
huṅkāragambhīrārāvaiḥ premāśrupulakairvṛtaḥ|
vrajan kramāttāmuttīrya vanaṁ cāgraṁ dadarśa ha||3||
verses.wbw: хункара-гамбхира-араваих — с глубокими раскатами возгласов «хум»; према-ашру-пулакаих — слезами любви и трепетом; вритах — объятый; враджан — идя; крамат — постепенно; там — её (Ямуну); уттирья — переправившись; ванам — лес; ча — и; аграм — Агры; дадарша — увидел; ха — же.
notes: Чтение и понимание этого места предположительны: возможно также «и увидел лес впереди».

verses.text: Там есть селение по имени Ренука — место великого душой сына Джамадагни, владыки воинов<sup>*</sup>; в это святое место Он затем и пришёл.
verses.orig:
तत्रैव रेणुका नाम ग्रामो यत्र युधां पतिः।
जामदग्निर्महात्मा च पुण्यक्षेत्रे ययौ ततः॥४॥
verses.translit:
tatraiva reṇukā nāma grāmo yatra yudhāṁ patiḥ|
jāmadagnirmahātmā ca puṇyakṣetre yayau tataḥ||4||
verses.wbw: татра эва — там же; ренука — Ренука; нама — по имени; грамах — селение; йатра — где; юдхам — воинов; патих — владыка; джамадагних — сын Джамадагни; маха-атма — великий душой; ча — и; пунья-кшетре — в святое место; йайау — пошёл; татах — затем.
notes: Сын Джамадагни — Парашурама; Ренука, мать Парашурамы, дала имя селению (ныне Рунакта близ Агры).

verses.text: Там Он увидел Ямуну, вечно обращённую к лесу Вринды; затем пришёл в Раджаграму<sup>*</sup> и, увидев Гокулу, был вне Себя.
verses.orig:
तत्रैव यमुनां दृष्ट्वा वृन्दारण्योन्मुखीं सदा।
राजग्रामं ततो गत्वा गोकुलं प्रेक्ष्य विह्वलः॥५॥
verses.translit:
tatraiva yamunāṁ dṛṣṭvā vṛndāraṇyonmukhīṁ sadā|
rājagrāmaṁ tato gatvā gokulaṁ prekṣya vihvalaḥ||5||
verses.wbw: татра эва — там же; ямунам — Ямуну; дриштва — увидев; вринда-аранья-унмукхим — обращённую к лесу Вринды; сада — всегда; раджа-грамам — в Раджаграму; татах — затем; гатва — придя; гокулам — Гокулу; прекшья — увидев; вихвалах — вне себя.
notes: Раджаграма — селение на пути к Гокуле; точное местоположение неясно.

verses.text: Созерцая Махаранью<sup>*</sup>, Он увидел и Матхуру — царскую столицу, исполненную великого величия и несказанно прекрасную,
verses.orig:
महारण्यं च संपश्यन् मथुरां च ददर्श ह।
राजधानीं महैश्वर्ययुक्तां परमशोभनाम्॥६॥
verses.translit:
mahāraṇyaṁ ca saṁpaśyan mathurāṁ ca dadarśa ha|
rājadhānīṁ mahaiśvaryayuktāṁ paramaśobhanām||6||
verses.wbw: маха-аранйам — Махаранью (Великий лес); ча — и; сампашьян — созерцая; матхурам — Матхуру; ча — и; дадарша — увидел; ха — же; раджадханим — столицу; маха-аишварья-юктам — исполненную великого величия; парама-шобханам — несказанно прекрасную.
notes: Махаранья («Великий лес») — Махавана, где находится Гокула.

verses.text: высший предмет поклонения на земле даже для Шри Вайкунтхи и прочих обителей, место явления Шри Кришны, дарующее любовную преданность.
verses.orig:
श्रीवैकुण्ठादिधाम्नां हि परमाराधनं भुवि।
श्रीकृष्णप्रकटं चापि प्रेमभक्तिप्रदायिनीम्॥७॥
verses.translit:
śrīvaikuṇṭhādidhāmnāṁ hi paramārādhanaṁ bhuvi|
śrīkṛṣṇaprakaṭaṁ cāpi premabhaktipradāyinīm||7||
verses.wbw: шри-ваикунтха-ади-дхамнам — Шри Вайкунтхи и прочих обителей; хи — поистине; парама-арадханам — высший предмет поклонения; бхуви — на земле; шри-кришна-пракатам — место явления Шри Кришны; ча апи — а также; према-бхакти-прадайиним — дарующую любовную преданность.

verses.text: Увидев её, Гаурахари, охваченный всеми преображениями любви, смеялся, плясал, плакал, катался по земле, и всё тело Его трепетало.
verses.orig:
दृष्ट्वा गौरहरिः प्रेमविकारसर्वसंयुतः।
हसन् नृत्यन् रुदन् भूमौ विलुठन् पुलकाचितः॥८॥
verses.translit:
dṛṣṭvā gaurahariḥ premavikārasarvasaṁyutaḥ|
hasan nṛtyan rudan bhūmau viluṭhan pulakācitaḥ||8||
verses.wbw: дриштва — увидев; гаура-харих — Гаурахари; према-викара-сарва-самьютах — охваченный всеми преображениями любви; хасан — смеясь; нритьян — пляша; рудан — плача; бхумау — по земле; вилутхан — катаясь; пулака-ачитах — покрытый трепетом.

verses_en.text: With deep rumbling cries, wrapped in tears of love and thrills of rapture, He went on and on, and having crossed the Yamuna He saw the forest of Agra<sup>*</sup>.
verses_en.orig:
हुङ्कारगम्भीरारावैः प्रेमाश्रुपुलकैर्वृतः।
व्रजन् क्रमात्तामुत्तीर्य वनं चाग्रं ददर्श ह॥३॥
verses_en.translit:
huṅkāragambhīrārāvaiḥ premāśrupulakairvṛtaḥ|
vrajan kramāttāmuttīrya vanaṁ cāgraṁ dadarśa ha||3||
verses_en.wbw: hunkara-gambhira-aravaih — with deep rumbling cries of "hum"; prema-ashru-pulakaih — with tears of love and thrills; vritah — enveloped; vrajan — going on; kramat — by stages; tam — her (the Yamuna); uttirya — crossing; vanam — the forest; cha — and; agram — of Agra; dadarsha — saw; ha — indeed.
notes: Both the reading and the sense of this place are conjectural; it may also mean "and saw a forest ahead."

verses_en.text: There lies a village named Renuka, the home of the great-souled son of Jamadagni, the lord of warriors<sup>*</sup>; to that holy place He then went.
verses_en.orig:
तत्रैव रेणुका नाम ग्रामो यत्र युधां पतिः।
जामदग्निर्महात्मा च पुण्यक्षेत्रे ययौ ततः॥४॥
verses_en.translit:
tatraiva reṇukā nāma grāmo yatra yudhāṁ patiḥ|
jāmadagnirmahātmā ca puṇyakṣetre yayau tataḥ||4||
verses_en.wbw: tatra eva — right there; renuka — Renuka; nama — by name; gramah — a village; yatra — where; yudham — of warriors; patih — the lord; jamadagnih — the son of Jamadagni; maha-atma — great-souled; cha — and; punya-kshetre — to the holy place; yayau — went; tatah — then.
notes: The son of Jamadagni is Parashurama; Renuka, Parashurama's mother, gave her name to the village (now Runakta near Agra).

verses_en.text: There He saw the Yamuna, ever turned toward the forest of Vrinda; then He came to Rajagrama<sup>*</sup> and, beholding Gokula, was overwhelmed.
verses_en.orig:
तत्रैव यमुनां दृष्ट्वा वृन्दारण्योन्मुखीं सदा।
राजग्रामं ततो गत्वा गोकुलं प्रेक्ष्य विह्वलः॥५॥
verses_en.translit:
tatraiva yamunāṁ dṛṣṭvā vṛndāraṇyonmukhīṁ sadā|
rājagrāmaṁ tato gatvā gokulaṁ prekṣya vihvalaḥ||5||
verses_en.wbw: tatra eva — right there; yamunam — the Yamuna; drishtva — seeing; vrinda-aranya-unmukhim — turned toward the forest of Vrinda; sada — ever; raja-gramam — to Rajagrama; tatah — then; gatva — going; gokulam — Gokula; prekshya — beholding; vihvalah — overwhelmed.
notes: Rajagrama: a village on the way to Gokula; its exact location is uncertain.

verses_en.text: Beholding Maharanya<sup>*</sup>, He saw Mathura too — the royal capital, endowed with great majesty and supremely beautiful,
verses_en.orig:
महारण्यं च संपश्यन् मथुरां च ददर्श ह।
राजधानीं महैश्वर्ययुक्तां परमशोभनाम्॥६॥
verses_en.translit:
mahāraṇyaṁ ca saṁpaśyan mathurāṁ ca dadarśa ha|
rājadhānīṁ mahaiśvaryayuktāṁ paramaśobhanām||6||
verses_en.wbw: maha-aranyam — the Great Forest (Mahavana); cha — and; sampashyan — beholding; mathuram — Mathura; cha — and; dadarsha — saw; ha — indeed; rajadhanim — the royal capital; maha-aishvarya-yuktam — endowed with great majesty; parama-shobhanam — supremely beautiful.
notes: Maharanya ("the Great Forest"): Mahavana, where Gokula lies.

verses_en.text: the supreme object of worship on earth even for Sri Vaikuntha and the other abodes, the place where Sri Krishna appeared, the bestower of loving devotion.
verses_en.orig:
श्रीवैकुण्ठादिधाम्नां हि परमाराधनं भुवि।
श्रीकृष्णप्रकटं चापि प्रेमभक्तिप्रदायिनीम्॥७॥
verses_en.translit:
śrīvaikuṇṭhādidhāmnāṁ hi paramārādhanaṁ bhuvi|
śrīkṛṣṇaprakaṭaṁ cāpi premabhaktipradāyinīm||7||
verses_en.wbw: shri-vaikuntha-adi-dhamnam — of Sri Vaikuntha and the other abodes; hi — indeed; parama-aradhanam — the supreme object of worship; bhuvi — on earth; shri-krishna-prakatam — the place where Sri Krishna appeared; cha api — and also; prema-bhakti-pradayinim — bestowing loving devotion.

verses_en.text: At the sight of it Gaurahari, possessed by every transformation of love, laughed, danced, wept and rolled on the ground, His whole body thrilling.
verses_en.orig:
दृष्ट्वा गौरहरिः प्रेमविकारसर्वसंयुतः।
हसन् नृत्यन् रुदन् भूमौ विलुठन् पुलकाचितः॥८॥
verses_en.translit:
dṛṣṭvā gaurahariḥ premavikārasarvasaṁyutaḥ|
hasan nṛtyan rudan bhūmau viluṭhan pulakācitaḥ||8||
verses_en.wbw: drishtva — seeing; gaura-harih — Gaurahari; prema-vikara-sarva-samyutah — possessed by all the transformations of love; hasan — laughing; nrityan — dancing; rudan — weeping; bhumau — on the ground; viluthan — rolling; pulaka-achitah — covered with thrills.

gaura-krishnodaya.title: Матхура: экстаз Господа; брахман — ученик Мадхавендры
gaura-krishnodaya.summary: Во Врадже Господь пляшет в слезах; омывшись у Вишрамы, видит Кешаву на месте рождения; брахман-ученик Мадхавендры принимает Его, и с ним Господь обходит святыни Матхуры.

verses.text: Через несколько дней Он достиг желанной Враджи; жители смотрели на Него не мигая, а Он, увидев сладость Мадху-пури [Матхуры], плясал в слезах премы, с волосами, вставшими дыбом.
Взволнованный, омывшись однажды в святыне Вишрамы на Ямуне, придя во внешнее сознание, Он вместе с горожанами увидел Кешаву, прекрасно наряженного, в храме на месте Его рождения.
Увидев Его, словно чудо, некий брахман из Матхуры, ученик Мадхавендры в той лесной стране, с радостью, почитая [Его] как гуру, привёл Господа к себе домой и накормил.<sup>*</sup>
notes: ЧЧ Мадхья 17: брахман-санодия, ученик Мадхавендры Пури, стал проводником Господа по Матхуре.

verses.text:
Обрадованный его преданностью, Он с горожанами, одаряя их ласковыми словами, радостно умножая богатство премы, изумил сердца движущихся и неподвижных существ.
[с. 68]
Осмотрев с этим брахманом из Матхуры многие святыни Матхуры, Он, желая увидеть лес Шри Вриндавана, отправился в путь, орошая слезами каждый шаг.

verses_en.text: After a few days He reached the longed-for Vraja; its people gazed at Him without blinking, and He, seeing the sweetness of Madhu-puri [Mathura], danced in tears of prema, His hair standing on end.

Agitated, having once bathed at the holy place of Vishrama on the Yamuna, on coming to external consciousness He, together with the townspeople, saw Keshava, beautifully dressed, in the temple at the place of His birth.
Seeing Him as a wonder, a certain brahmin of Mathura, a disciple of Madhavendra in that forest land, joyfully, honouring [Him] as a guru, brought the Lord to his home and fed Him.<sup>*</sup>
notes: CC Madhya 17: a Sanodiya brahmin, a disciple of Madhavendra Puri, became the Lord's guide in Mathura.

verses_en.text:
Pleased with his devotion, He, with the townspeople, favouring them with kind words and joyfully increasing the wealth of prema, amazed the hearts of moving and non-moving beings.
[p. 68]
Having seen with that brahmin of Mathura the many holy places of Mathura, He, wishing to see the forest of Sri Vrindavana, set out, watering every step with tears.

lochana-cm.title: От Праяги к Матхуре: Ренука, Гокула; Господь три дня без чувств в разлуке
lochana-cm.summary: Омывшись в Тривени и увидев Акшая-ват, Господь переправляется через Ямуну у Агры, проходит Ренуку, видит из Раджаграмы Гокулу и Махавану; увидев Матхуру, Он с криком «Акрура!» падает без чувств в бхаве разлуки и три дня лежит без сознания.

verses.text:
Там, совершив омовение в Вени и увидев Акшая-ват,
Он переправился через Ямуну близ Агры.
verses.orig:
তথা বেণী-স্নান করি' দেখি' অক্ষয়বট ।
যমুনাতে পার হৈলা আগরা নিকট ॥ ৩৯ ॥
verses.translit:
tathā beṇī-snāna kari' dekhi' akṣaẏabaṭa |
yamunāte pāra hailā āgarā nikaṭa || 39 ||
verses.wbw: татха вени-снана кари — там, совершив омовение в Вени; декхи акшаявата — увидев Акшая-ват; ямунате пара хаила — переправился через Ямуну; агара никата — близ Агры

verses.text:
Он увидел дивную деревню по имени Ренука —
место, где явился Парашурама.
verses.orig:
দেখিলা অদ্ভুত সে রেণুকা নামে গ্রাম ।
অবতার কৈলা যেই স্থানে পরশুরাম ॥ ৪০ ॥
verses.translit:
dekhilā adbhuta se reṇukā nāme grāma |
abatāra kailā yei sthāne paraśurāma || 40 ||
verses.wbw: декхила адбхута — увидел дивную; се ренука наме грама — деревню по имени Ренука; аватара каила — явился; йеи стхане парашурама — в каком месте Парашурама

verses.text:
Там Ямуна, повернув [вспять], обращена к Вриндавану;
видя это, Господь, вне Себя, счастлив счастьем премы*.
verses.orig:
তথা বৃন্দাবন-মুখে যমুনা বিমুখী ।
দেখিয়া বিহ্বল প্রভু প্রেমসুখে সুখী ॥ ৪১ ॥
verses.translit:
tathā bṛndābana-mukhe yamunā bimukhī |
dekhiẏā bihbala prabhu premasukhe sukhī || 41 ||
verses.wbw: татха — там; вриндавана-мукхе — обращённая к Вриндавану; ямуна вимукхи — Ямуна, повернувшая [вспять]; декхия — видя; вихвала прабху — Господь вне Себя; према-сукхе сукхи — счастлив счастьем премы
notes: Ст. 39–45 — ср. Мурари 4.02.2–6. Акшая-ват — «нетленный баньян» в Праяге; Вени (Тривени) — слияние Ганги, Ямуны и Сарасвати. Ст. 41 понимаем, как у Мурари (4.02.5): Ямуна «вечно обращена к лесу Вринды».

verses.text:
Придя в Раджаграму, Он видит Гокулу на другом берегу;
не в силах сдержать сердце, Он пришёл в смятение.
verses.orig:
রাজগ্রামে গিয়া পারে দেখয়ে গোকুল ।
সম্বরিতে নারে হিয়া ভৈ গেল আকুল ॥ ৪২ ॥
verses.translit:
rājagrāme giẏā pāre dekhaẏe gokula |
sambarite nāre hiẏā bhai gela ākula || 42 ||
verses.wbw: раджаграме гия — придя в Раджаграму; паре декхайе гокула — видит Гокулу на другом берегу; самбарите наре хия — не может сдержать сердце; бхаи гела акула — пришёл в смятение

verses.text:
С великим усилием Господь сдержал сердце;
вне Себя от блаженства, Он видит на другом берегу Махавану.
verses.orig:
হিয়া সম্বরিল প্রভু অনেক যতনে ।
আনন্দে বিহ্বল পারে দেখে মহাবনে ॥ ৪৩ ॥
verses.translit:
hiẏā sambarila prabhu aneka yatane |
ānande bihbala pāre dekhe mahābane || 43 ||
verses.wbw: хия самбарила прабху — Господь сдержал сердце; анека ятане — с великим усилием; ананде вихвала — вне Себя от блаженства; паре декхе махаване — видит Махавану на другом берегу

verses.text:
Шёл Он, шёл ещё немало —
и, приблизившись, видит Мадхупуру.
verses.orig:
যাইতে যাইতে আর গিয়া কথোদূর ।
সুনিকট হৈল যেই দেখে মধুপুর ॥ ৪৪ ॥
verses.translit:
yāite yāite āra giẏā kathodūra |
sunikaṭa haila yei dekhe madhupura || 44 ||
verses.wbw: яите яите — идя и идя; ара гия катходура — пройдя ещё немало; суниката хаила — приблизился; йеи декхе мадхупура — и видит Мадхупуру

verses.text:
Увидев Мадхупуру, Господь обезумел сердцем;
обессилев от премы, Он словно лишился сознания.
verses.orig:
মধুপুর দেখি' প্রভু উনমত-চিত ।
প্রেমায় বিহ্বল যেন নাহিক সম্বিত ॥ ৪৫ ॥
verses.translit:
madhupura dekhi' prabhu unamata-cita |
premāẏa bihbala yena nāhika sambita || 45 ||
verses.wbw: мадхупура декхи — увидев Мадхупуру; прабху унамата-чита — Господь обезумел сердцем; премая вихвала — обессилев от премы; йена нахика самвита — словно нет сознания

verses.text:
«Акрура! Акрура!» — воскликнув, Он упал на землю;
в бхаве разлуки, [когда Кришна ушёл в] Матхуру, Он лишился чувств*.
verses.orig:
অক্রূর অক্রূর বলি' ভূমিতে পড়িলা ।
মাথুর-বিরহ-ভাবে মূর্ছিত হইলা ॥ ৪৬ ॥
verses.translit:
akrūra akrūra bali' bhūmite paṛilā |
māthura-biraha-bhābe mūrchita hailā || 46 ||
verses.wbw: акрура акрура бали — восклицая «Акрура! Акрура!»; бхумите падила — упал на землю; матхура-вираха-бхаве — в бхаве разлуки [с Кришной, ушедшим в] Матхуру; мурчхита хаила — лишился чувств
notes: Акрура увёз Кришну из Враджа в Матхуру, и гопи в разлуке винили его. Господь, увидев Матхуру, переживает разлуку гопи (Радхи) с Кришной.

verses.text: Не различая дня и ночи, Он остаётся на том месте;
verses.orig:
দিবানিশি নাহি জানে আছে সেইখানে ।
সম্বেদন নাহি প্রভুর ভেল তিন দিনে ॥ ৪৭ ॥
verses.translit:
dibāniśi nāhi jāne āche seikhāne |
sambedana nāhi prabhura bhela tina dine || 47 ||
verses.wbw: диваниши нахи джане — не различает дня и ночи; ачхе сеикхане — остаётся там; самбедана нахи прабхура — нет у Господа сознания; бхела тина дине — три дня

verses_en.text:
There, bathing at the Veni and seeing the Akshaya-vata,
He crossed the Yamuna near Agra.
verses_en.orig:
তথা বেণী-স্নান করি' দেখি' অক্ষয়বট ।
যমুনাতে পার হৈলা আগরা নিকট ॥ ৩৯ ॥
verses_en.translit:
tathā beṇī-snāna kari' dekhi' akṣaẏabaṭa |
yamunāte pāra hailā āgarā nikaṭa || 39 ||
verses_en.wbw: tatha veni-snana kari — there, bathing at the Veni; dekhi akshayavata — seeing the Akshaya-vata; yamunate para haila — crossed the Yamuna; agara nikata — near Agra

verses_en.text:
He saw a wondrous village named Renuka —
the place where Parashurama appeared.
verses_en.orig:
দেখিলা অদ্ভুত সে রেণুকা নামে গ্রাম ।
অবতার কৈলা যেই স্থানে পরশুরাম ॥ ৪০ ॥
verses_en.translit:
dekhilā adbhuta se reṇukā nāme grāma |
abatāra kailā yei sthāne paraśurāma || 40 ||
verses_en.wbw: dekhila adbhuta — He saw a wondrous; se renuka name grama — village named Renuka; avatara kaila — appeared; yei sthane parashurama — the place where Parashurama

verses_en.text:
There the Yamuna, turning [back], faces Vrindavana;
seeing this, the Lord, beside Himself, is happy with the happiness of prema*.
verses_en.orig:
তথা বৃন্দাবন-মুখে যমুনা বিমুখী ।
দেখিয়া বিহ্বল প্রভু প্রেমসুখে সুখী ॥ ৪১ ॥
verses_en.translit:
tathā bṛndābana-mukhe yamunā bimukhī |
dekhiẏā bihbala prabhu premasukhe sukhī || 41 ||
verses_en.wbw: tatha — there; vrindavana-mukhe — facing Vrindavana; yamuna vimukhi — the Yamuna, turned [back]; dekhiya — seeing; vihvala prabhu — the Lord beside Himself; prema-sukhe sukhi — happy with the happiness of prema
notes: Vv. 39–45 — cf. Murari 4.02.2–6. The Akshaya-vata is the "imperishable banyan" at Prayaga; the Veni (Triveni) is the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and Sarasvati. V. 41 we understand as in Murari (4.02.5): the Yamuna "ever turned towards the forest of Vrinda."

verses_en.text:
Coming to Rajagrama, He sees Gokula on the far bank;
unable to restrain His heart, He became distraught.
verses_en.orig:
রাজগ্রামে গিয়া পারে দেখয়ে গোকুল ।
সম্বরিতে নারে হিয়া ভৈ গেল আকুল ॥ ৪২ ॥
verses_en.translit:
rājagrāme giẏā pāre dekhaẏe gokula |
sambarite nāre hiẏā bhai gela ākula || 42 ||
verses_en.wbw: rajagrame giya — coming to Rajagrama; pare dekhaye gokula — sees Gokula on the far bank; sambarite nare hiya — cannot restrain His heart; bhai gela akula — became distraught

verses_en.text:
With great effort the Lord restrained His heart;
overwhelmed with bliss, He sees Mahavana on the far bank.
verses_en.orig:
হিয়া সম্বরিল প্রভু অনেক যতনে ।
আনন্দে বিহ্বল পারে দেখে মহাবনে ॥ ৪৩ ॥
verses_en.translit:
hiẏā sambarila prabhu aneka yatane |
ānande bihbala pāre dekhe mahābane || 43 ||
verses_en.wbw: hiya sambarila prabhu — the Lord restrained His heart; aneka yatane — with great effort; anande vihvala — overwhelmed with bliss; pare dekhe mahavane — sees Mahavana on the far bank

verses_en.text:
He went on and on some distance more —
and, drawing near, He sees Madhupura.
verses_en.orig:
যাইতে যাইতে আর গিয়া কথোদূর ।
সুনিকট হৈল যেই দেখে মধুপুর ॥ ৪৪ ॥
verses_en.translit:
yāite yāite āra giẏā kathodūra |
sunikaṭa haila yei dekhe madhupura || 44 ||
verses_en.wbw: yaite yaite — going and going; ara giya kathodura — going some distance more; sunikata haila — He drew near; yei dekhe madhupura — and sees Madhupura

verses_en.text:
Seeing Madhupura, the Lord became mad at heart;
overcome with prema, He seemed to lose consciousness.
verses_en.orig:
মধুপুর দেখি' প্রভু উনমত-চিত ।
প্রেমায় বিহ্বল যেন নাহিক সম্বিত ॥ ৪৫ ॥
verses_en.translit:
madhupura dekhi' prabhu unamata-cita |
premāẏa bihbala yena nāhika sambita || 45 ||
verses_en.wbw: madhupura dekhi — seeing Madhupura; prabhu unamata-chita — the Lord mad at heart; premaya vihvala — overcome with prema; yena nahika samvita — as if without consciousness

verses_en.text:
Crying "Akrura! Akrura!", He fell to the ground;
in the bhava of separation, [when Krishna left for] Mathura, He fainted*.
verses_en.orig:
অক্রূর অক্রূর বলি' ভূমিতে পড়িলা ।
মাথুর-বিরহ-ভাবে মূর্ছিত হইলা ॥ ৪৬ ॥
verses_en.translit:
akrūra akrūra bali' bhūmite paṛilā |
māthura-biraha-bhābe mūrchita hailā || 46 ||
verses_en.wbw: akrura akrura bali — crying "Akrura! Akrura!"; bhumite padila — fell to the ground; mathura-viraha-bhave — in the bhava of separation [when Krishna left for] Mathura; murchhita haila — fainted
notes: Akrura took Krishna away from Vraja to Mathura, and the gopis in separation blamed him. Seeing Mathura, the Lord lives through the separation of the gopis (of Radha) from Krishna.

verses_en.text: Not knowing day or night, He remains in that place;
verses_en.orig:
দিবানিশি নাহি জানে আছে সেইখানে ।
সম্বেদন নাহি প্রভুর ভেল তিন দিনে ॥ ৪৭ ॥
verses_en.translit:
dibāniśi nāhi jāne āche seikhāne |
sambedana nāhi prabhura bhela tina dine || 47 ||
verses_en.wbw: divanishi nahi jane — knows not day or night; achhe seikhane — remains there; sambedana nahi prabhura — the Lord had no consciousness; bhela tina dine — for three days

bhakti-ratnakara.title: Путь Махапрабху из Праяги через Гокулу-Махавану и Равал в Матхуру
bhakti-ratnakara.summary: Из Праяги Господь дошёл до Аграваны, затем в Ренуку — ашрам Джамадагни, через Раджаграм пришёл в Гокулу и сидел под древним деревом; с толпой и нама-санкиртаной пошёл к месту рождения Кришны в Махаване, танцевал под песни праздника рождения и, увидев Мадана-гопала, потерял самообладание; люди говорили: «Это не санньяси — это Кришна». Из Гокулы Он со спутниками пришёл в Равал, где Его экстаз не описать, и оттуда с брахманом-санодией отправился в Матхуру.

verses.text:
О Шриниваса, Кришна Чайтанья здесь,
увидев, как поют [песни] праздника рождения, возрадовался сердцем.*
notes: В изд. 1960 г. «জন্মোৎসব-স্থান» — «увидев место праздника рождения».

verses.text:
В упоении чувств Господь погрузился в танец и пение;
по Своей милости Он привлёк все сердца.

Видя Господа, люди сбегаются со всех четырёх сторон;
потеряв самообладание, они восклицают: «Хари! Хари!»

У всех из глаз непрестанно льются слёзы;
все говорят: «Это не санньяси — это, несомненно, Кришна».

Обезумев от премы к Господу, все люди
говорят так многое и падают, катаясь по земле.

Кто в силах понять пути Шри Гаурачандры?
В Махаване разлился великий океан блаженства.
Увидев Мадана-гопала, [Господь] потерял самообладание;<sup>*</sup>
notes: Мадана-гопал (ниже, 1784, — Мадана-мохан) — Божество, которому служил Санатана Госвами; позднее Он был установлен во Вриндаване.

verses.text:
О Шриниваса, это дерево — древнее;
взгляни на красоту этого дерева: её не описать.

Жители Гокулы обретают здесь прохладу;
Гауранга, придя в Гокулу, сидел именно здесь.

Как Господь пришёл сюда —
кто сможет описать это подробно?

Из Праяги, постепенно дойдя до Аграваны,
Он вскоре прибыл в ашрам Джамадагни.*
notes: Агравана — лес, по-видимому, у нынешней Агры. Джамадагни — мудрец, отец Парашурамы.

verses.text:
Его жена — Ренука; селение называется Ренука —
[там], где родился Шри Парашурама.*
notes: Ренука — селение у Ямуны (вероятно, нынешняя Рунакта близ Агры), названное по имени жены Джамадагни, матери Парашурамы.

verses.text:
Из Ренуки быстро, через Раджаграм,
придя в Гокулу, Он остановился под этим деревом.*
notes: Раджаграм — селение на пути из Ренуки в Гокулу.

verses.text:
Так [сказано] в «Шри Чайтанья-чарите», в четвёртой пракраме, во второй сарге:*
«Затем, придя в Праягу и увидев Господа Шри Мадхаву,
исполненный нектара блаженства премы, Он танцевал вместе со Своими спутниками.
notes: «Шри Чайтанья-чарита» — санскритская поэма Мурари Гупты («Шри Кришна-чайтанья-чаритамрита»). «Во второй сарге» — по изд. 1912/13 г.; в изд. 1960 г. во вводной строке только «в четвёртой пракраме». Шри Мадхава — Божество Вени-мадхавы в Праяге (ср. ЧЧ Мадхья 17).

verses.text:
Увидев славный Акшая-ват и совершив омовение в Тривени,
окунувшись в Ямуну с игривостью опьянённого слона,*
notes: Акшая-ват («неистребимый баньян») — священный баньян в Праяге; Тривени — слияние Ганги, Ямуны и Сарасвати там же.

verses.text:
с глубокими громовыми кличами-хункарами, весь в слезах премы и трепете,
идя [дальше], Он постепенно переправился через неё и увидел Агравану.

Там же — селение по имени Ренука, где владыка воителей
и великий душой Джамадагни нисошли на эту святую землю.*
notes: В изд. 1960 г. «জামদগ্ন্যো মহাত্মা চ» — «великий душой сын Джамадагни», т. е. владыка воителей — это сам Парашурама.

verses.text:
Там же, увидев Ямуну, всегда устремлённую к Вриндавану,
а затем придя в Раджаграм и узрев Гокулу, Он был вне Себя».
Здесь, в великом упоении нама-санкиртаной,

О Шриниваса, Гаурачандра со Своими спутниками,
придя из Гокулы, остановился здесь.

Каким было [Его] погружение в экстаз, когда Он увидел селение Равал, —
что уж говорить о других: даже Шеша не в силах это описать.

Со всех четырёх сторон сбегаются люди, восклицают имя Хари;
все говорят: «Смотри, брат, — Венец санньяси!»

Опьянённый питьём нектара луны лица Господа,
кто-то, ликуя, говорит кому-то:

«Я рассудил в уме: это, несомненно, Кришна;
в этом облике Он по Своей воле странствует во Врадже».

Кто-то говорит: «При виде этого золотого тела
не выходит на уста то, что [у меня] на сердце».

Говоря так многое, люди по милости Чайтаньи
не в силах сохранить самообладания — из глаз [их] льются потоки.
Явив здесь неземную игру, Господь

verses_en.text:
O Srinivasa, Krishna Chaitanya here,
seeing how [the songs of] the birth festival were sung, rejoiced at heart.*
notes: The 1960 ed. reads "জন্মোৎসব-স্থান" — "seeing the place of the birth festival".

verses_en.text:
In a rapture of feeling the Lord became absorbed in dancing and singing;
by His mercy He drew all hearts.

Seeing the Lord, people come running from all four directions;
losing their composure, they cry out, "Hari! Hari!"

From everyone's eyes tears flow ceaselessly;
all say, "This is no sannyasi — this is certainly Krishna."

Maddened by prema for the Lord, all the people
say so much and fall rolling on the ground.

Who has the power to understand the ways of Sri Gaurachandra?
In Mahavana a great ocean of bliss arose.
Seeing Madana-gopala, [the Lord] lost His composure;<sup>*</sup>
notes: Madana-gopala (below, in 1784, Madanamohana) is the Deity served by Sanatana Gosvami; later He was installed in Vrindavana.

verses_en.text:
O Srinivasa, this tree is ancient;
look at the beauty of this tree: it cannot be described.

The residents of Gokula find refreshment here;
Gauranga, coming to Gokula, sat right here.

How the Lord came here —
who could describe it in detail?

From Prayaga, gradually reaching Agravana,
He soon arrived at the ashrama of Jamadagni.*
notes: Agravana is a forest, apparently near present-day Agra. Jamadagni is a sage, the father of Parashurama.

verses_en.text:
His wife was Renuka; the village is named Renuka —
[the place] where Sri Parashurama took birth.*
notes: Renuka is a village by the Yamuna (probably present-day Runakta near Agra), named after Jamadagni's wife, the mother of Parashurama.

verses_en.text:
From Renuka, quickly, by way of Rajagrama,
coming to Gokula, He stayed under this tree.*
notes: Rajagrama is a village on the way from Renuka to Gokula.

verses_en.text:
Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-charita, in the fourth prakrama, in the second sarga:*
"Then, coming to Prayaga and seeing the Lord Sri Madhava,
filled with the nectar of the bliss of prema, He danced together with His companions.
notes: The Sri Chaitanya-charita is the Sanskrit poem of Murari Gupta (Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita). "In the second sarga" follows the 1912/13 ed.; in the 1960 ed. the introductory line has only "in the fourth prakrama". Sri Madhava is the Deity of Veni-madhava at Prayaga (cf. CC Madhya 17).

verses_en.text:
Seeing the glorious Akshaya-vata and bathing at the Triveni,
plunging into the Yamuna with the playfulness of an intoxicated elephant,*
notes: Akshaya-vata ("the imperishable banyan") is the sacred banyan at Prayaga; the Triveni is the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and Sarasvati there.

verses_en.text:
with deep, thunderous roars of hunkara, covered with tears of prema and thrills,
proceeding [onward], He gradually crossed it and saw Agravana.

There too is the village named Renuka, where the lord of warriors
and the great-souled Jamadagni descended upon this holy land.*
notes: The 1960 ed. reads "জামদগ্ন্যো মহাত্মা চ" — "the great-souled son of Jamadagni", i.e. the lord of warriors is Parashurama himself.

verses_en.text:
There, seeing the Yamuna, which ever flows toward Vrindavana,
and then going to Rajagrama and beholding Gokula, He was beside Himself."
Here, in great rapture in nama-sankirtana,

O Srinivasa, Gaurachandra with His associates,
coming from Gokula, stayed here.

How deep was [His] absorption in ecstasy on seeing the village of Raval —
what to speak of others, even Shesha cannot describe it.

From all four sides people come running and raise the name of Hari;
all say, "Look, brother — the Crest-jewel of sannyasis!"

Drunk with drinking the nectar of the moon of the Lord's face,
someone, rejoicing, says to someone else:

"I have concluded in my mind: this is surely Krishna;
in this guise He wanders in Vraja by His own will."

Someone says, "On seeing this golden form,
what is in [my] heart does not come to my lips."

Saying so much, the people, by Chaitanya's mercy,
cannot keep the strength of composure — streams pour from their eyes.
Having manifested a wondrous pastime here, the Lord

advaita-prakasha.title: Матхура: «Где Кану?»; Господь ищет Камсу; Дхрува-гхат
advaita-prakasha.summary: В Матхуре, в настроении гопи, Господь поёт: «Где Кану?» и катается по земле, затем, в бхаве Своих игр, ищет Камсу, рычит и хлопает по рукам; на Дхрува-гхате плачет, вспоминая Дхруву.

verses.text: Постепенно Гаура пришёл в округ Матхуры и, охваченный настроением гопи, забыл Себя.
«Где Кану, где Кану, где Мне Его найти? Утешу ли жизнь, сожжённую огнём разлуки?»
Распевая этот стих, Он онемел и только плакал, повторяя: «Где? Где?»
В таком состоянии у Горы прошла вторая стража; наконец Он стал кататься по земле, так что людям стало страшно.
Через некоторое время, в экстазе Своих собственных игр, Гора бродил туда и сюда, ища Камсу.
Он рычал по-львиному, хлопал себя по рукам, подпрыгивал вверх — кто постигнет Его ум?
Так в Нём вспыхивали разные чувства, и день и ночь прошли, словно один миг.
Затем Шачинандана пришёл на Дхрува-гхат и, вспоминая историю Дхрувы, заплакал.
Увидев скопление людей, Он сдержал любовь, омылся и узрел Божество.

verses_en.text: Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Sitanatha! Glory to Nityananda-Rama together with the devotees!
One day Sri Krishna Chaitanya secretly told the devotees: "I shall go to Vrindavana."
The devotees replied: "It is now the rainy season; to go to Vraja-dhama now, as we see it, is not good."
The word of saintly Vaishnavas is a great god: by transgressing it one destroys all good.
Having said this, Gaura accepted the devotees' word and set out with His own for His homeland.
He stayed at the Acharya's house in Shantipura; seeing Gaura, the Lord was overcome with love.
Now He roared, now danced wildly, saying again and again: "What good fortune for Me today!"
Of Mother Sita's love one cannot even speak: with the Ganga water of her eyes she bathed Gora's whole body.
Sita's sons were very mighty; of them, on the path of devotion, three were foremost:
Sri Achyuta, Krishna Mishra and Sri Gopaladasa — the Lord rejoiced in the beautiful character of these three.
Their lives were always given to Gaura; seeing Gauranga, they bathed in the nectar of love.
They sang the Name loudly, surpassing the Gandharvas, and at times, intoxicated with love, they roared.
With arms outspread Gaura and Nityananda danced, and all the devotees sang a great sankirtana.
I bathed in the nectar Ganga of seeing Him, and by the good fortune of millions of lives I devoted myself to service.
Mother Sita cooked dishes surpassing nectar and with the devotees served the three Thakuras.
What bliss there was cannot be told: only one who is most fortunate receives such maha-prasada.
Receiving the good news of Sri Gauranga's coming, Mother Shachi came joyfully to Shantipura.
Seeing His mother, Gora prostrated Himself before her, and Shachi-devi took Him in her arms with love.
As Krishna at Kurukshetra in the arms of Yashoda — the same feeling arose in the lotuses of the devotees' hearts.
Who, seeing such a pastime, could remain calm? All hearts were drawn to the shore of the ocean of love.
Then Shachi cooked various dishes, everything Sri Gauranga loved, and bathua greens,
gourd, kalai, sweet rice, cakes and drinks — all surpassing nectar, beyond compare.
Sri Krishna Chaitanya sat down to eat: on the right Nitai, on the left the blessed Sri Advaita.
Mahaprabhu said: "The greens are best of all." Nityananda said: "Something else would be better."
Gaura, laughing, said to Lord Nityananda: "Your love, like the Ganga, flows towards the low."
Nityananda replied: "Your head is turned upwards — how can You see the low, but only the high?"
Then all three Thakuras laughed loudly; only the greatly fortunate grasped even a shadow of the meaning.
Mother kept perfecting her service, and every day there was a festival in the Lord's house.
After some days Sri Chaitanya, the great Lord, set out hastily, saying: "I shall go to Vraja."
In due course He came to the village of Ramakeli and there met Rupa and Sanatana.
Sri Rupa and Sanatana are treasuries of all learning, royal ministers equal in intellect to Brihaspati.
Mahaprabhu showed them great mercy, and, giving up worldly pleasures, both became free from envy.
Sri Chaitanya said: "I shall go to Vrindavana." Rupa and Sanatana privately dissuaded Him.
Both said: "Listen, Mahaprabhu, ocean of mercy: never go (there) with a crowd of people."
At the devotees' word Sri Gauranga turned south and after some days arrived at Shantipura.
With Gaura's coming the bliss of love surged up, and my Lord held a festival of sankirtana.
There Gora met Mother Shachi and, receiving her permission to go to Vraja, set out south (for Puri).
On the way He met Raghunatha Dasa, whose worship amazes the sadhus.
In the waves of fragrance of the wish-fulfilling sandal tree, Gaura, the poison of his worldly enjoyment easily vanished.
Mahaprabhu praised his detachment; that truth I cannot describe.
One day Sri Chaitanya came to Kshetra-dhama and, seeing Jagannatha, melted with the sweetness of love.
Seeing Gaura, the devotees became intoxicated with bliss and held a great festival of the sankirtana of the Name.
After some days Sriman Gaura Vishvambhara firmly resolved to go to Vrindavana.
One day at the end of the night Gora, in a hidden ecstasy of mahabhava, set out for Vraja-dhama.
Leaving the main road, He went by a by-way — through the Jharikhanda forest, to the people's amazement.
He loudly sang the sankirtana of the name of Hari, and on seeing Gaura the beasts gave up their ferocity.
Mahaprabhu said: "Hey, beasts of the forest! Weep, crying 'Krishna,' and all your bonds will be broken."
The command of Bhagavan Himself is surely effective: in love the beasts, crying "Krishna," wept.
In the dense forest a great festival began: by the power of the Name all the beasts and birds were liberated.
What can I say of the greatness of Sri Chaitanya's mercy? By the name of Hari even the immobile beings were liberated in this life.
The pastimes of Sri Krishna Chaitanya are a great ocean of jewels: neither the Four-faced One nor others find their beginning or end.
I, a most insignificant creature, know nothing: for my heart's joy I only briefly enumerate the essence.
The ignorant do not believe this at all; know for certain: it is accessible to the wise.
What to speak of the pastimes of Bhagavan Himself — the divine power of a devotee is seen with one's own eyes only by good fortune.
Mahaprabhu went on, preaching the Name; on the way He made many people Vaishnavas, imparting power to them.
After some days Gaura came to Kashi and bathed in the Ganga at the Manikarnika ghat.
There Tapana Mishra, seeing Sri Gauranga, prostrated himself with the eight limbs of his body in great bliss.
With entreaties he took Him to his house, and Gaurachandra stayed there several days.
Then Gora, beholding Bindu-Madhava, raised His arms and danced wondrously.
Restraining His love, He prostrated Himself and offered manifold praises, like Ananta himself.
Seeing Vishveshvara, Gora was filled with love and only repeated with His lips: "Hari-Hara, Hari-Hara."
Bowing to Shiva, He recited a divine hymn, as Brahma recites the Vedas with his four mouths.
Unearthly is Gora's love, unearthly His form; seeing it, all said: "This is the emperor of sadhakas."
Then Sri Chaitanya, seeing Annapurna, intoxicated with love, called her Paurnamasi.
Now He laughed, now wept, now fainted, now with a roar danced round about.
Seeing this, the people of Kashi were amazed; some said: "This is the incarnation of a god."
Then Mishra took Him to his house and offered Mahaprabhu food with various gifts.
With all his kin he partook of the maha-prasada; there also Gora met Chandrashekhara.
Then Sri Gauranga, beholding the Deity of Adi-Keshava, was lost in pure love.
Thus, having held a festival in Kashi, Gaura Hari went from there to Sri Prayaga.
Seeing the Triveni, He was overcome with love and only called out: "Daughter of Kalinda (Yamuna)!"
"What good fortune — I have seen the Yamuna!" With this cry He plunged into the water.
All day Gora remained under the water of the Yamuna, and in the evening, out of mercy, He surfaced.
Fishermen lifted Him into a boat, and, sitting in the boat, Gora sang the sankirtana of Hari.
All were enchanted by that sweet singing, and Gora, greatly delighted, came out onto the bank.
At the time of the evening arati Shachinandana, seeing Madhava, wept with love.
Raising His arms, Gora roared and said again and again: "Give bhakti! Give bhakti!"
He danced wondrously, as people had never seen; at the manifold love of Gauranga all things moving and unmoving wept.
After a long time Gora restrained His love; seeing the Bhima-ganga, He grew merry.
Then from Sri Prayaga He went along the road to Vrindavana, delivering the souls by the gift of the treasure of love.
In due course Gaura came to the district of Mathura and, overwhelmed by the mood of the gopis, forgot Himself.
"Where is Kanu, where is Kanu, where shall I find Him? Shall I comfort a life scorched by the fire of separation?"
Singing this verse, He became speechless and only wept, repeating: "Where? Where?"
In this state the second watch passed for Gora; at last He began to roll on the ground, so that people were frightened.
After some time, in the ecstasy of His own pastimes, Gora wandered hither and thither looking for Kamsa.
He roared like a lion, slapped His arms, leaped upwards — who can fathom His mind?
Thus various moods flared up in Him, and day and night passed like a single moment.
Then Shachinandana came to the Dhruva-ghat and, remembering the story of Dhruva, wept.
Seeing the crowd of people, He restrained His love, bathed and beheld the Deity.
Then Mahaprabhu came to holy Vrindavana; as soon as He reached Vraja, He fainted with love.
After a long time Sri Gauranga came to Himself, but, repeating only "Here, here," became speechless.
Tirelessly He rolled in the spiritual dust and in mahabhava called out: "Where is My beloved?"
"Where is Kanu, where is Kanu?" He called again and again; day and night He searched for Krishna.
Streams of love flowed ceaselessly from both His eyes; at times, weeping loudly, He wandered from forest to forest.
At times He laughed loudly for a whole watch, at times He roared like a lion — who can fathom the end of it?
Mahaprabhu's mahabhava is inaccessible even to the gods — who has the power to describe it?
Gora wandered along the paths of Vraja and every moment repeated: "Say 'Krishna,' say 'Krishna.'"
At the command of Sri Krishna Chaitanya all things unmoving and moving, like Ananta, cried: "Krishna, Krishna!"
At that time cows and calves surrounded Gaura and began to lick Gaura's body, fragrant with Krishna.
Tasting the nectar Ganga, Gauranga, the cows wept in a great ecstasy of love.
Seeing this, Gora said: "Inconceivable is the nature of Vraja: the people of Vraja have an innate love for Krishna."
Having said this, He placed His lotus hand on the bodies of all, and the cows danced like the gopis of Vraja.
At the dance of the cows and calves Gora's love overflowed, and, crying "hai-hai," He danced like one intoxicated.
Meanwhile Sri Achyutananda, the son of Advaita, was searching for Gora as if mad with love.
Now, crying "Where is Gora?", he roared; now, crying "Sri Gauranga!", he wept uncontrollably.
Now he said: "Where is my Gorachand, my life?" Gauranga learned of the sorrow of His dear devotee.
"Come, come!" — saying this, Gora drew him, and Sita's son, like a yogi, appeared there.
From Shantipura to Vraja is a journey of many days; Achyuta came on the flower-chariot of Gora's command.
Krishna and the devotees of Krishna have inconceivable power: everything is possible, there is nothing astonishing in it.
Seeing Gauranga, Achyuta said loudly: "Hey, Gora, You have taken away my life and come to a distant land!
Leaving the Vraja of devotion, You have come to the Vraja of the gopis. Will You go to the Vraja of devotion, or worship in the love of the gopis?"
Although the Vraja of the gopis is eternally full of bliss, its highest part is the Vraja of devotion.
"For Your sake Sri Yashoda and the other people of Vraja have manifested the Vraja of devotion in Navadvipa.
In what ecstasy have You come to the deserted Vraja of the gopis? To learn this I have come to You."
Sri Gauranga said: "You are the best of bhagavatas: in all beings Sri Krishna appears to you.
In the ecstasy of love you speak so much nonsense! You call empty the place of the eternal pastimes of Radha and Krishna!"
Sri Achyuta replied: "Radha and Krishna united — for the sake of what desire have You now become one body?
The divine form which Ananta and the others have not seen has, by the good fortune of millions of lives, appeared before me.
And yet I called Vrindavana empty — I have committed a great offence; forgive it out of Your goodness."
Gora said: "An eternally perfect devotee of Krishna sees the holy form of Radha and Krishna everywhere.
Krishna regards him as dearer than life and never takes account of his offences.
You are an intimate, eternal devotee of Krishna: in your company love has flared up in Me."
Sri Achyuta said: "Your command is the great Veda; Your most pure mercy makes no distinction between souls.
It is mercy that makes You speak humbly; Your glory is known only to one in whom there is pure devotion.
I am insignificant and know nothing of the true essence; I count only the shelter of Your feet as my great good fortune."
Gora said: "You have deep love for Krishna: by touching your body a soul becomes fortunate."
Having said this, Sri Chaitanya embraced Achyuta, held him tight and in love repeated: "Hari, Hari!"
Sri Achyuta, overcome with love for Gaura, in the mood of a sakhi danced and sang like one intoxicated.
Then Sri Chaitanya remembered Radha-kunda and in the ecstasy of love asked everyone: "Where is Radha-kunda?"
The people of Vraja replied that no one knew; hearing this, Gora fell senseless on the spot.
Seeing Gauranga's mahabhava, Achyuta called the names of Radha and Krishna, and tears flowed from both his eyes.
Hearing the name of Radha, Gora rose with a roar and wept: "Where is Radha-kunda?"
Sri Achyuta said: "Dear Sri Krishna Chaitanya, hear from me the hidden truth about Radha-kunda."
Gora said: "You are an eternal companion of Krishna: the spiritual holy places and sacred sites are known to you."
Sri Achyuta said: "I bow to Your mercy: You always exalt the honour of Your devotees.
You have resolved to reveal to the world two great holy places and to proclaim the omniscience of Your devotee.
The kunda of the Mistress of the kunda has inconceivable power; the same power surely belongs to Shyama-kunda.
Ananta and the other gods find no limit to the two — how should insignificant I know of them?
Know me as a wooden puppet: as You wish, so I dance.
My teacher is Your beloved Gadadhara, Pandita Gosvami, a treasury of love.
My father calls him a part of Sri Radhika: in his company devotion to Krishna is attained.
He mercifully told me these words; I speak them, not knowing whether it is good or bad.
Where Radha, the Mistress of the kunda, eternally abides, that is Sri Radha-kunda — this is the evident proof.
Who knows the limit of the glory of Sri Radha-kunda? She is the very presiding essence of all holy places.
All the holy places, washing away the sins of sinners, themselves bear the heap of those sins;
in the company of saints those sins are destroyed — so say the shrutis: the holiness of the holy places comes from them.
Radha-kunda is the spiritual potency of Krishna, an eternally perfect reality, the shelter of all potencies.
Remembering Sri Radha-kunda destroys all sins; telling of her gives faith in the eternal dharma.
Seeing Sri Kunda gives a sprout of devotion; by a mere touch loving devotion awakens.
Bathing in the waters of the Kunda surely leads to Krishna; whoever leaves the body on her bank obtains the service of Krishna.
Who can list the countless virtues of Sri Kunda? Hear now of some of her secondary virtues.
All the beings living on the bank of the Kunda are perfected souls: hearing the names of Radha and Krishna, they weep.
Merely seeing Sri Kunda heals one's sufferings: the world is forgotten, and jubilation grows in the mind.
Her very water is sweet, like medicine: bathing in it and drinking it prolong life and cure diseases.
Beside Sri Kunda is beautiful Shyama-kunda: like Radha-kunda, it is dear to Krishna and spiritual.
There Sri Nandanandana eternally abides; at the sight of it the form of Krishna is revealed.
Even Sri Ananta does not know its glory: bathing in it and drinking it grant Radha and Krishna."
Having said this, Sri Achyuta bowed to Gaura, and Gora in the ecstasy of love embraced him tightly.
Gora said: "Today I have heard of the glory of Sri Kunda — I consider My body, life and mind blessed."
Having said this, He went on in the ecstasy of mahabhava and came to the almost vanished Radha-kunda.
Sri Krishna Chaitanya said to the Acharya's son: "This is Radha-kunda — look at the signs.
Although this great holy place has almost vanished, at the sight of it the sorrow of the mind has passed.
Why has the jubilation of love suddenly risen so?" Having said this, He cried with a roar: "Radha!"
Hearing the name of Radha, all the beasts and birds wept in the ecstasy of love, like the best devotees of Krishna.
The name of Radha by itself eternally gives rise to bliss — and here it fell from Gaura's lips, full of true love!
Hearing that sound, in whom would love not awaken? In the bliss of love tears flowed from the moving and the unmoving.
Sri Gauranga said: "Look, son of the Acharya: by the name of Radha love has awakened in every soul.
This is the true Radha-kunda, there is no doubt; and the pond adjoining it is Shyama-kunda.
What good fortune — I have seen Sri Kunda! Such is the divine, inconceivable virtue of the company of saints."
Having said this, the all-knowing Lord, intoxicated with the nectar of love, leaped into the water.
Having dipped in Radha-kunda, He crossed to Shyama-kunda, bathed in Shyama-kunda and returned to Radha-kunda.
Having finished His bath, Gora took clay from the Kunda and, overwhelmed with love, smeared it all over His body.
With deep love Gaura Hari prostrated Himself a hundred times and offered the Kunda manifold praises.
Seeing this, Sri Achyuta, intoxicated with love, wandered about roaring: "This is the spiritual Kunda!"
Then Mahaprabhu, in the mood of Radha, the Mistress of the kunda, wept aloud: "Where is the Lord of My life?"
Now stupor, now trembling, now loud laughter, now a roar, now dancing, now humble speech.
The waves of the great ocean of love rose ever higher, and Sri Chaitanya fell senseless to the ground.
Seeing Gauranga's motionless body, Sri Achyuta wept ceaselessly: "Ah, Gaura, my life!"
After some time Sita's son grew a little calmer and in a deep voice began to cry: "Hari, Hari!"
In the third watch Gora came to Himself and broke into dance: "I have found Radha-kunda!"
The two kundas that belong to those Two — He, seeing the terrible age of Kali, mercifully joined and revealed.
Then Gaurachandra, taking Achyuta by the hand, went round the Kunda, reciting the great mantra.
Again and again, hundreds of times, He prostrated Himself; Sri Achyuta in the ecstasy of love bathed in the Kunda.
Hearing his insistent, devoted, humble words, Gora grew a little calmer and sat down under a tree.
Gauranga said: "Achyuta, by the virtue of association with you Radha-kunda has mercifully appeared."
Achyuta replied: "Why do You make me an offender? I eternally abide in the shelter of Your feet.
Age after age You display unearthly pastimes: to deliver the souls You have revealed a hidden holy place.
The hidden love, the hidden Kunda had long been concealed; by Your mercy Radha-kunda has appeared."
Hearing this, Mahaprabhu said: "This is excessive praise. It is his father's dharma — I do not like it.
Krishna alone is the Lord of all, and all others are servants: to see Ishvara in a soul is utter ruin."
Sri Achyuta replied: "By the law of Your pastimes You speak humbly, to conceal the truth about Yourself.
As a cloud cannot hide the sun, so in His manifest pastimes Krishna cannot remain hidden."
Having said this, Sri Achyuta cried out the name of Hari. Gora said: "The Name alone is true — leave other talk."
Sri Achyuta replied: "The Possessor of the Name I have obtained by the good fortune of millions of lives," — and, clasping Gora's feet, he wept.
Then Gora, the ocean of mercy, showed mercy and revealed to him His own perfect form — the Divine Couple.
The form of Sri Krishna, the King of rasas, the most complete; and at His left the form of Radha, mahabhava.
Seeing these two eternal forms, Sri Achyuta, overcome with love, prostrated himself.
He offered manifold praises, composing verses. Gora said: "Why do you praise Me?"
Seeing Gaura again in the form of a sannyasi, Sri Achyuta said: "You have hidden Your form in the body of Radha.
Well: by serving You the service of the Couple is accomplished" — and, having said this, he placed Gaura's lotus feet on his head.
Gora said: "You are an emperor of love for Krishna: wherever you are, Radha and Krishna appear to you."
Having said this, Sri Chaitanya embraced him, and Sri Achyuta broke into dance in the bliss of love.
When the news of the Kunda became known to all the people, they were purified by bathing in it, drinking from it and seeing it.
Then Mahaprabhu went to Govardhana Hill; seeing the hill of the pastimes, He fainted with love.
Coming to Himself, He said: "O best of hills, without Krishna your body has grown old, it seems."
And again He said: "What a wonder I see — ah, ah! The scent of Krishna's body has remained on you.
Come, let Me embrace you and comfort My scorched life; and then I shall go, if I find the Beloved of My life."
Having said this, Sri Chaitanya, with arms outspread, ran to embrace Govardhana Hill.
Now falling, now rising, dancing wherever He was, the Lord went round it, singing the name of Hari.
Unearthly is Gora's love, inconceivable His pastimes: distributing the nectar of mercy, He delivered the souls.
Sri Achyutananda, lost in love, now wept, now danced, now rolled on the ground.
Then Gauranga went round all the forests and holy places; at the sight of the place of the rasa dance His love leaped up.
In mahabhava, imagining that Krishna had disappeared, Gora recited the Gopi-gita and wandered about in tears.
Now He imitated the pastimes of Radha and Krishna, now sang songs, now danced.
The love of Sri Gauranga is an assemblage of great oceans: even Sri Ananta is unable to describe it.
I am a fool, an insignificant worm, I know nothing: I enumerate only the essence from the words of saintly Vaishnavas.
Although Gaura did not wish to leave Vraja, at the wish of the devotees He left it, shedding tears.
Placing his hope in the feet of Sri Chaitanya and Sri Advaita, Ishana Nagara tells the Advaita-prakasha.
